summary: Intermittent throughput collapse with pod evictions and long-tail latency on dedicated reservation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Acme Analytics, dedicated reservation) reported intermittent severe throughput drops and elevated p95/p99 token latency beginning 2026-03-09. Sessions see sustained 504s or streaming disconnects for ~30-90s windows.

Impact:
- Multiple production endpoints for Acme experienced request timeouts and 5xx errors during windows.
- Observed end-to-end p95 increased from ~280ms to >3.2s during events; tail hits 10s+.
- Customer SLA: dedicated latency SLO breached; risk of production downtime for key features.

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU reservation: res-acme-us-east (NVIDIA A10G equivalent), autoscaler policy: min_replicas=1, max_replicas=10, scale_up_threshold=65% GPU utilization, scale_down_threshold=30%
- Runtime version: serving-runtime v2.14.1; autoscaler v1.8.0; scheduler v3.2.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Normal traffic baseline for customer for hours.
2) At T0 a background tenant job on the same reservation begins (large-batch client job).
3) Within ~45–90s GPU SM/utilization climbs to >95%, kernel queue length spikes.
4) Serving pods begin to queue; requests hit request queueing timeout and backend returns 504s.
5) Autoscaler does not scale up fast enough due to conservative scale_up_threshold and min_replicas=1; scale-up completes after ~120–200s.
6) During scale-up pods experience GPU eviction signals (kube OOM & device preemption logs), causing additional retry storms.

Observations / logs (high-level):
- Prometheus: GPU SM utilization shows step-change from 40% -> 96% aligned to event windows.
- Scheduler metrics: kernel_queue_length metric elevated to 18–24 for affected GPUs.
- Kube events: multiple Pod eviction events: "DevicePreemption: MIG/eviction-triggered"  (12 evictions in 5m).
- Serving logs: request handler backlog warnings and intermittent "failed to allocate CUDA memory" traces.
- Traces: downstream retries amplify client-side concurrency causing head-of-line blocking.

Hypotheses tested so far:
- Noisy neighbor: confirmed a non-customer batch job (internal CI job from team-data) began large throughput runs coincident with incidents. Logs show job ID ci-batch-887 ramped GPU load.
- Autoscale mis-sizing: min_replicas=1 and scale_up_threshold=65% caused slow reaction to rapid utilization spikes.
- Eviction amplification: when preemption events occur, pods restart and trigger kube-scheduler binpacking which can cause temporary localized hotspots.

Investigation notes / timeline:
- 2026-03-09 10:12 UTC: First customer Slack (Acme) ping to #support reporting elevated timeouts.
- 2026-03-09 10:18 UTC: SRE observed correlated GPU utilization spikes; created this ticket.
- 2026-03-09 10:30 UTC: Identified internal CI job (ci-batch-887) running on same reservation; asked infra-team to terminate.
- 2026-03-09 10:34 UTC: CI job terminated; metrics returned to baseline within ~90s and customer traffic recovered.
- 2026-03-10 02:40 UTC: Repeat occurrence; further analysis showed autoscaler scale-up latency ~160s due to kube-provisioner delays and pod scheduling backpressure.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Shifted Acme traffic to warm spare reservation res-acme-us-east-b in same region at 2026-03-09 10:40 UTC (manual routing override).
- Bumped reservation min_replicas to 3 for res-acme-us-east to reduce single-point scaling delay.
- Applied node taint for internal CI jobs to avoid landing on reserved pools.

Root-cause (current working):
Primary cause is noisy-neighbor background GPU batch workload occupying SM capacity on the shared dedicated reservation combined with autoscaler policy that is too conservative for rapid bursts. Device preemption/evictions during high contention amplified scheduling instability and restart churn, creating a feedback loop that prolonged throughput degradation.

Next steps / action items (owners):
- (infra) Enforce placement constraints so internal CI and non-dedicated batch jobs cannot schedule on customer-dedicated reservations. Target: 2026-03-13. (Assignee: Priya Nair).
- (autoscale) Update autoscaler policy templates for dedicated reservations: recommend min_replicas >= 2 and lower scale_up_threshold to 50% for bursty customers; add faster scale-up ephemeral slots. Target: 2026-03-16. (Assignee: Leo Martin).
- (scheduler) Investigate pod scheduling latency and reduce provisioning jitter; implement soft-eviction fallback policy to reduce restart storms. Target: 2026-03-20. (Assignee: Jamal Ortiz).
- (SRE/Support) Run retrospective and publish runbook for noisy-tenant detection and automated migration. Target: 2026-03-18. (Assignee: Maya Chen).

Workaround communicated to customer:
- We temporarily routed production traffic to an alternate reservation and increased min_replicas to reduce scale-up dependency. Customer accepted temporary routing and will monitor traffic for 72 hours.

Resolution notes (future):
- Pending: formal config changes to autoscaler and infra placement policy. Once completed, we'll schedule a controlled rollback of temporary routing to original reservation and monitor for recurrence for 7 days.
